cards.text: Paul is writing to the church in Thessalonica, with Silvanus and Timothy right beside him (2 Thess 1:1). He just finished praying for these believers, asking God to encourage their hearts (2 Thess 2:16-17). Now he starts wrapping up with 'Finally, brothers,' and friend, I say 'finally' at the oven every night, and somehow there's ALWAYS three more batches.

cards.question: Paul just prayed for the believers in Thessalonica. Now that he's wrapping up, what does he ask them to do for him and his team?

cards.text: And look at the first thing on Paul's list. It's not a nicer bed or a smoother road. It's the word of the Lord.

cards.question: Paul asks the believers in Thessalonica to pray about the word of the Lord. What does he want to happen with it?

answers.text: It spreads quickly and is honored
It stays hidden until the right time
It is kept among the church leaders

cards.question: Paul says the word of the Lord was already held in honor among the believers in Thessalonica.

cards.text: Then comes prayer request number two. This one is about Paul's team staying safe while they're out there sharing that word.

cards.question: Paul asks the believers to pray that his team will be delivered from wicked and evil ___.
Paul explains why his team runs into wicked and evil men: not everyone holds to the ___.

cards.text: Not everyone holds to the faith. Then Paul turns it around: 'But the Lord is faithful.' Baker, that's my whole junk drawer story in five words. Everybody forgot about me. HE didn't.

cards.question: Paul says the Lord is faithful. What does he say the Lord will do for the believers in Thessalonica?

answers.text: Strengthen and guard them from the evil one
Take away every trouble in their lives
Bring Paul back to stay with them

cards.text: Next, Paul tells the believers he's confident about them. But watch where he puts that confidence.

cards.question: Paul says his confidence is in the ___ that the believers will do what he commands.
Paul says the believers in Thessalonica are already doing what he commands, not just that they will someday.

cards.text: Confidence in the Lord, not in their willpower. Smart. I put my confidence in MY willpower once. The snooze button won. Eleven times. ELEVEN.
These believers have been enduring persecutions and afflictions (2 Thess 1:4). So Paul closes with a prayer for their hearts: 'May the Lord direct your hearts…'

cards.question: Paul prays the Lord will direct the hurting believers' hearts into something of Christ's. What is it?
Paul also prays the Lord will direct the believers' hearts into God's love.

findings.problem: The card says the prayer for deliverance is about the team staying safe 'while they're out there sharing that word.' Verse 2 never links the deliverance request to spreading the word. It is a separate request, so the card adds a connection the text leaves open.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to guess the next word of 'wicked and evil ___' (men, spirits or beasts). That is wording the baker hasn't seen, and card 6 ('staying safe') gives nothing to reason from. 'Spirits' is also easy to argue for, since verse 3 names 'the evil one.' This makes the card a guess about the wording, not a reasoned pick.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The card opens with 'Not everyone holds to the faith,' which retells 2 Thessalonians 3:2, but it cites only 2 Thessalonians 3:3. It should cite 2 Thessalonians 3:2-3.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The statement contrasts 'already doing' with 'they will someday.' Verse 4 says 'will continue to do,' which means ongoing, not someday. The card adds a time the text doesn't give.

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: The card says 'So Paul closes with a prayer for their hearts,' which presents the persecutions of 1:4 as Paul's reason for the prayer in 3:5. The text gives no reason for this prayer.

rule.text: Reasons: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: The card says Paul 'closes with' the prayer in 3:5. The letter goes on through 2 Thessalonians 3:18, so this prayer doesn't close it.

rule.text: Retelling: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: The question calls them 'the hurting believers,' which states a feeling as fact. Neither verse 5 nor 1:4 says they are hurting.

rule.text: Feelings: He can guess at a feeling, marked as his own ("I think," "I bet"). Never as fact.
